Encode Glycans with GlycanGT

fp_glycangt.Rd

Returns 768-dimensional graph Transformer embeddings from the official GlycanGT large mask-35 model using a manually supplied local checkpoint.

Usage

fp_glycangt(glycans, checkpoint, ..., na_action = "propagate")

Arguments

glycans

A glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector or a character vector in any format supported by glyparse::auto_parse(). Formats are detected automatically, as in glymotif. For explicit format selection, use the corresponding glyparse parser first. Structures must be complete: concrete residues, specified linkages, positions, substituents and reducing-end alpha/beta state. Unknown or ambiguous fields raise an error.

checkpoint

Local path to the official pretrained_tokengt_large_multitask_mask_35_final.pt artifact. Obtain it from Akikitani295/GlycanGT. The file is identified by SHA-256, regardless of filename, and is never replaced or downloaded. A local checkpoint is required on every call.

...

Reserved for future options. Must be empty.

na_action

"propagate" (default) returns an all-NA vector for each missing input; "error" rejects missing inputs.

Value

A list of named double vectors with 768 coordinates (glycangt_001 to glycangt_768), preserving input length, order and names. Missing inputs return all-NA vectors with the full coordinate set. No model object is returned.

Details

GlycanGT returns the model's final graph token and requires at least two residues. Its orthogonal random identifiers use master seed 1729, a SHA-256-derived seed per canonical projected glycan, the official single-graph Gaussian QR construction and width 64. This fixed policy preserves caller R and CPU torch RNG state. Upstream multi-graph ORF batches can yield different outputs; this adapter does not claim to reproduce published downstream performance.

Embedding contract

Pretrained models do not encode reducing-end alpha/beta information: only after complete-structure validation, preprocessing omits this known state at the normal reducing carbon. Thus embeddings cannot distinguish glycans differing only in this state; motif fingerprints retain it. Other reducing-end positions and unsupported chemistry are rejected. Tokens outside the fixed model vocabulary always raise an error.

Embeddings run in R with optional torch and digest; SweetNet and GlycanGT also use zip. No Python, RDKit or GlyLES runtime is used. Install torch's runtime explicitly: loading glyfp and calling inference never install it automatically. CPU evaluation uses float32, frozen normalization, no dropout or gradients, and one glycan at a time. Batch order, duplicates and batch size do not change coordinates under the same model, weights, preprocessing and runtime settings. Preserve these settings and package/runtime versions with saved results. Cross-platform comparisons should allow floating-point tolerance (the reference tests bound maximum absolute coordinate error by 1e-5).

Complete structures

All fingerprint functions validate complete input structures. Missing inputs are distinct from unknown structure fields: empty input returns list() and missing inputs retain the full coordinate set filled with NA values. Recompute compared vectors when the model, dictionary or implementation changes.

See also

fp_motif_count(), fp_sweetnet(), fp_gifflar()

Examples

checkpoint <- Sys.getenv("GLYFP_TEST_GLYCANGT_CHECKPOINT")
if (file.exists(checkpoint) && requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE) &&
    torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  fp <- fp_glycangt("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", checkpoint = checkpoint)
  lengths(fp)
}
